changes.current_line: Support plans with tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage.
changes.change: For event and peak-driven merchants, and especially their operations buyers (COO), stop describing 'tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage' and say instead: 'A name, not a queue.' You get a named account owner, a named escalation path, and someone on the line live during your on-sale windows. 'Someone who picks up.' Name the actual people in the pitch.
changes.why: When the COO asked for a person, our tier and response-time pitch read to her as 'a queue with a faster timer', which is what she was leaving, and the customer's own words were 'A name, not a queue', 'Someone who picks up' and 'who's my person'.

changes.change: Add a reusable peak-event plan as a proof asset for ticketing and other event merchants: a one-page written runbook for an on-sale morning covering who is watching, who the customer calls, and what we do in the first minutes after payments start failing. Offer it unprompted to the operations buyer, built with the solutions engineer for each deal.
changes.why: The decider asked to see 'on paper, what we do on an on-sale morning', the rep said 'We don't have that as a thing', and the triggering incident was payments failing 'about four minutes in'.

changes.change: Add an opener for operations buyers at event merchants that leads with incident response, not uptime or platform scale: 'I don't buy uptime, I buy what happens when it's down.' Then answer it directly: when payments fail on 'On-sale morning', here is who is already watching and who picks up.
changes.why: The COO said 'I don't buy uptime, I buy what happens when it's down', and the switch was triggered when the CEO saw a public failure that the old provider's ticket form answered only after the on-sale was over.

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: For event and ticketing prospects, pair the logo proof with a ticketing reference customer who will speak to the operations buyer about who answered during a live on-sale, not about platform features.
changes.why: The rep said 'I had logos. I didn't have a person.', and the decider made 'her call' in one meeting where a person-based story beat our logo-based proof.
